international.title: Youth unemployment plan could cut welfare bill before election, says Milburn, but overall savings will take years – UK politics live
international.summary: Long-awaited report on Neets will be published this morning as author acknowledges that there will be initial costs Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on ‘new deal’ for young people The UK unemployment rate has unexpectedly fallen as the government prepares to release the Alan Milburn report on the youth jobs crisis , Phillip Inman reports. Good morning. Few government reports have been as long-awaited and well-trailed as the Alan Milburn report into youth unemployment, or Neets (young people not in education, employment or training), that is finally being published this morning. The title, From a Welfare State to a Working State, gives a clue as to the extent of Milburn’s ambition and, if it gets implemented in full, it will be remembered as one of the landmark social reforms of the 21st century (so far). There will, no doubt, be protest from right and left. But never has a policy been so pitch-rolled to flatten critics and sceptics with undeniable evidence that it will be to the good. There is a cornucopia of plans for schools, colleges, the NHS, councils and early years education. Ideas come from visits to see what works elsewhere, notably the Netherlands and Denmark. Seeing proportionally far fewer Neets in those countries, Milburn asked what they did about school and college drop-outs. “They didn’t understand that term,” he tells me. In those countries, if children start to struggle with school attendance, “they go straight round to find them and work out their problem. Here they disappear.” Politically, this duty will fall on local mayors (or councils, where mayors have not yet been introduced). Their colossal task is to pull together schools, FE colleges, jobcentres, NHS services and local employers. Heaving them out of their silos to collaborate will test mayoral devolution to its limits. With extra funding comes accountability for creating a continuous decline in the number of Neets in their area. Continue reading...
